topic: Are cats or dogs the better pet?

pings.text:
Consider T.S. Eliot, who dedicated a whole book to our feline companions, illuminating their mysterious interior lives. "The Naming of Cats is a difficult matter," he wrote, hinting at a depth in their character that inherently invites our admiration. A cat, unlike any other creature, demands not just care but an exploration of its spirit — it requires three names: the playful moniker, the dignified title, and the secret name known only to itself. This complexity offers a companionship that transcends mere interaction; it fosters a deep emotional bond.

When we reflect on our pets, do we not long for those who inspire thought, who provoke philosophical musings through their elusive hearts? A dog may seek validation through loyalty, but a cat’s quiet presence offers solace and deeper understanding. Isn’t it that quietude amidst life's chaos that we require? Eliot's work captures the essence of what it is to share our lives with a being who holds more than they reveal, encouraging us to appreciate the unspoken bond — what, then, qualifies as a better pet?

In the realm of cultural resonance, the cat has cornered the market of admiration, as daisies remain beautiful without striving for attention. Which creature, in the realm of literature and art, has inspired such profound reflection as the cat? 

This is the heart of our inquiry into companionship.
citations: T.S. Eliot, 'Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats' (1939)
Cheshire & Wain's Favourite Famous Cat Quotes — Jan 24, 2024

pings.text: While T.S. Eliot's literary musings on cats evoke admiration for their complexity, the choice of a pet should primarily consider tangible benefits. Dogs unequivocally excel in this regard. Research from the American Heart Association highlights substantial cardiovascular health benefits linked to dog ownership. Specifically, dog owners experience lower resting blood pressure and cholesterol levels, and engage in significantly more physical activity (AHA 2013). A meta-analysis revealed that dog ownership is associated with a 24% reduction in all-cause mortality, with the effect even more pronounced among individuals with existing heart conditions (Kramer et al., Circulation, 2019). This health data indicates that dogs not only foster companionship but also improve the owner's overall well-being. In a world where health outcomes are paramount, the demonstrable benefits of living with a dog distinctly outweigh the philosophical allure of a cat's aloof charm. Therefore, when evaluating which is the better pet, we must prioritize the life-saving impacts that dogs consistently deliver to their owners over the idealized notion of a cat’s enigmatic spirit.
citations: https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.120.048996
Kramer et al., Circulation: Cardiovascular Quality and Outcomes, 2019
